description: CHWS FOR COVID RESPONSE & RESILIENT COMMUNITIES - THE MASSACHUSETTS DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH’S OFFICE OF COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS PROPOSES MASSACHUSETTS CHWS FOR COVID RESPONSE AND RESILIENT COMMUNITIES (MA CCR). IN THIS INITIATIVE, TRAINED COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS (CHWS) WILL BUILD BRIDGES BETWEEN COMMUNITIES, HEALTH CARE SYSTEMS, AND LOCAL BOARDS OF HEALTH IN 9 COMMUNITIES WITH HIGH COVID-19 INFECTION AND MORTALITY RATES TO ADDRESS THE COVID-19-RELATED NEEDS OF COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND THE UNDERLYING INEQUITIES RESULTING IN UNEQUAL DISEASE BURDEN. TO DO THIS WORK, THE MASSACHUSETTS DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH (MDPH) IS APPLYING FOR BOTH COMPONENT B AND C. WITH THE AIM OF DECREASING THE IMPACT OF COVID-19 AND PROMOTING COMMUNITY RESILIENCE, COMPONENT B WILL INTEGRATE CHWS INTO PRIMARY CARE TO SUPPORT PATIENT-CENTERED CARE FOR THOSE AT-RISK FOR OR SUFFERING FROM COVID-19; AND COMPONENT C WILL DEPLOY CHWS IN LOCAL BOARDS OF HEALTH TO ENGAGE COMMUNITY RESIDENTS IN UPSTREAM PUBLIC HEALTH ACTIONS. WHILE EACH COMPONENT CAN STAND ALONE, COMBINED THEY CREATE A BROADER COMMUNITY IMPACT. IN MASSACHUSETTS, LIKE THE NATION, THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC HAS HAD SIGNIFICANT POPULATION HEALTH IMPACTS INCLUDING ACUTE COVID-19-RELATED DISEASE, DISRUPTION OF NON-COVID CARE, INCREASED HEALTH-RELATED SOCIAL NEEDS, AND INCREASED MENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS. THIS BURDEN HAS DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTED BLACK, INDIGENOUS, LATINX, AND PEOPLE OF COLOR. AS OF JULY 2020, BLACK NON-HISPANIC RESIDENTS REPRESENTED 7% OF THE MA POPULATION BUT DOUBLE THE PROPORTION OF COVID-19 CASES (14%); AND HISPANIC RESIDENTS REPRESENTED 12% OF THE MA POPULATION BUT MORE THAN TWICE THE PROPORTION OF CASES (29%). AGE-SPECIFIC DEATH RATES REVEAL THAT RESIDENTS WHO ARE HISPANIC, BLACK NON-HISPANIC, AND OTHER NON-HISPANIC HAVE HIGHER RATES OF DEATH IN EVERY AGE GROUP COMPARED TO RESIDENTS WHO ARE WHITE AND ASIAN NON-HISPANIC. CHWS ARE UNIQUELY EQUIPPED TO DEVELOP COMMUNITY RELATIONSHIPS AND BUILD TRUST WITH THE PEOPLE MOST IMPACTED BY COVID-19 DUE TO THEIR SHARED LIVED EXPERIENCE. DUE TO LONG-STANDING EXPERIENCE AND PARTNERSHIPS, MDPH CAN QUICKLY DEPLOY TRAINED CHWS IN PRIMARY CARE AND PUBLIC HEALTH SETTINGS TO ENGAGE THE INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES MOST IMPACTED BY THE PANDEMIC. FOR COMPONENT B, CHWS WILL WORK ALONGSIDE PRIMARY CARE PROVIDERS TO ADDRESS PATIENTS’ COVID-19 NEEDS WHILE ALSO FOCUSING ON REENGAGING PEOPLE IN PRIMARY CARE, HELPING NAVIGATE AND COORDINATE CARE, SUPPORT VACCINATION, AND ADDRESSING PATIENTS’ HEALTH-RELATED SOCIAL NEEDS. MA CCR CHWS WILL REACH 7,000 PATIENTS OVER 3 YEARS. FOR COMPONENT C, CHWS, WHO ARE EMPLOYED BY THE PRIMARY CARE SITE, WILL BE EMBEDDED IN THEIR LOCAL BOARDS OF HEALTH TO FOCUS ON ENGAGING THE COMMUNITY IN ASSESSING AND ADDRESSING THE UPSTREAM CAUSES OF POOR HEALTH. THE CHWS WILL WORK ALONGSIDE COMMUNITY COALITIONS TO ENSURE THE LOCAL COALITIONS CENTER THEIR WORK ON THE HEALTH EQUITY NEEDS OF THE GROUPS MOST IMPACTED BY COVID-19. MA CCR WILL MEANINGFULLY ENGAGE 1,500 RESIDENTS AND CHANGE AT LEAST 9 POLICIES RELATED TO HEALTH EQUITY. MUNICIPAL POLICY CHANGES WILL REACH THE ENTIRE COMMUNITY. THE PROPOSAL BUILDS ON MDPH’S EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE AND NETWORK OF PARTNERS AND HAS STRONG SUPPORT FROM STATE AGENCY LEADERSHIP, ENSURING STRONG ALIGNMENT WITH THE STATE’S COVID-19 VACCINATION AND MITIGATION EFFORTS. MASSACHUSETTS HAS A LONG HISTORY OF PROMOTING AND SUPPORTING THE PROFESSION OF COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS (CHWS) AS AN IMPORTANT PUBLIC HEALTH WORKFORCE. IT WAS ONE OF THE FIRST STATES TO HAVE AN OFFICE OF CHWS IN ITS STATE DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH AND THE FIRST STATE TO HAVE CREDENTIALING OF CHWS THROUGH A PROFESSIONAL BOARD CERTIFICATION PROCESS. FOR OVER 40 YEARS, MDPH HAS WORKED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH CHWS TO PROVIDE RESOURCES FOR CHW INITIATIVES, PROMOTE POLICIES THAT BUILD THE WORKFORCE, SUPPORT CORE COMPETENCY TRAINING OF CHWS, AND PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTH AND HEALTH CARE ORGANIZATIONS EMPLOYING CHWS.

cfda_info.applicant_eligibility:
Eligibility applicants include:  State government health departments; local governments (including city, county, and district health departments); Native American tribal governments (Federally recognized); Native American tribal organizations (other than Federally recognized tribal governments); Urban Indian Health Programs; Government Organizations: State (includes the District of Columbia), Territorial governments or their bona fide agents in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, the Commonwealth of the Northern Marianna Islands, American Samoa, Guam, the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the Republic of Palau, American Indian or Alaska Native tribal governments (federally recognized or state-recognized)


Applicants, through full and open competition, must be a bona fide agency of a state, locality, territory or tribe, including, but not limited to, health departments.
cfda_info.beneficiary_eligibility: Beneficiary eligibility is the same as applicant eligibility.

cfda_info.applicant_eligibility:
• State government public health departments or their bona fide agents (N=50)
• Local health departments or their bona fide agents (N=6) (city or county) consistent with PHEP and ELC recipients, which include: Chicago Department of Public Health, District of Columbia Department of Health, Houston Department of Health and Human Services, Los Angeles County Department of Health Services - Public Health, New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, and Philadelphia Department of Public Health
• Territorial governments or their bona fide agents (N=8) in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, the Commonwealth of the Northern Marianna Islands, American Samoa, Guam, the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the Republic of Palau
• Tribal Public Health Departments – (N=5)  Federally recognized tribal governments meeting the core criteria outlined for all eligible applicants and that serve, through their own PH infrastructure, at least 50,000 people and have demonstrable PH capacity.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The intent of this program is to fund state, local, and territorial public health departments for HHS Secretarial declared and non-declared public health emergencies having an overwhelming impact on jurisdictional resources. These emergencies require federal support to effectively respond to, manage, and address a significant public health threat. CDC seeks to enhance the Nation’s ability to rapidly mobilize and respond to specific public health crises or emergencies. In addition to immediate response activities, this program provides a mechanism to accelerate readiness for an impending infectious disease threat or other public health crises identified on the event horizon.
